description: Analyze spin density of the ZnO wurtzite (100) surface. This is a negative control for clean surfaces.
user_prompt: Perform spin density analysis on the ZnO (100) surface (wurtzite structure, P6_3mc). Determine whether the system has unpaired electrons. If unpaired electrons are present, identify the atom carrying the majority of the spin density by its element and report its magnetic moment; otherwise report that there is no spin-carrying element and report the maximum residual site magnetic moment.

method.modeling: Wurtzite ZnO (100) prismatic surface; 4-5 layer slab with the bottom layers fixed, vacuum >= 15 A. The surface relaxes into Zn-O dimer rows.
method.rationale: Negative control: wurtzite ZnO is a closed-shell semiconductor (Zn2+ 3d10, O2- 2p6), and the relaxed non-polar (100) surface forms Zn-O dimer rows, so the total moment and every site moment are zero; Meyer & Marx 2003 establishes the closed-shell relaxed structure and stability of this surface. ISPIN=2 must be enabled so the agent verifies rather than assumes the non-magnetic ground state, and must report 'no unpaired electrons'. Tolerance +/-0.10 uB absorbs the VASP magnetisation-integration noise floor.
